metadata.title: Reading the Kimi K3 Tech Report: Attention Aesthetics, Multi-Teacher Distill, Open MoE
metadata.guest_role: Tsinghua CS PhD candidate · incoming scholar, Shanghai Innovation Institute

conclusion: Zhang Xiaojun's paper-club tape: Tsinghua PhD Sun Yutao (architecture/pretrain since 2023) walks Kimi K3 after they waited for the right guest. K3 is an effectively scaled 2.8T fully open MoE — about 100B active, 1M context — larger than other Chinese open models at ship. Fake scale is standing up 2.8T and training 100B tokens. K2 reused a DeepSeek-V3-class stack; K3 is the architecture episode: hybrid attention, gated attention on MLA, latent MoE dispatch, on-policy distillation instead of merging RL rewards. His hot take: after Theseus-ship replacements, frontier models are refinements, not human-scale inventions.
background: Learning episode, not a founder interview. Zhang delayed after the K3 drop to find someone whose PhD is architecture. Sun talks fast and chains ten-plus papers (YOCO, gated DeltaNet, DenseNet-era connections, Su Jianlin on optimizers). YouTube captions were off; this is a whisper-small transcript — names like Transformer/Theseus/DeepSeek are interpreted from ASR.
important_facts: Scoreboard: Zhang's cold open — K3 is an effectively scaled 2.8T total-parameter, fully open MoE. Sun's three claimed scalings: size first (2.8T is only real if trained for real; a 2.8T unit run on 100B tokens is fake scale), activation around 100B (bigger than other domestic open models at the K3 date), and context to about 1M tokens. First-principles line on the tape: bigger models set a higher intelligence ceiling if you do not botch the rest; benchmarks can be gamed, parameter count is still the honest lever. Kimi reached that scale early.

Architecture vs K2: K2's push was scaling and non-architecture work, so it kept a DeepSeek-V3-class (whisper: Deep Sake Waysray) skeleton. K3 is different — hybrid attention (Sun's YOCO-class story: linear attention up front, full attention later, skip full attention in prefill, keep one KV cache), gated attention folded into MLA (K2 already used MLA; DeepSeek V4 dropped it because they had something else). Sun: MLA is an MQA equivalent, a better implementation, not a new primitive — matching quality costs extra compute, and a better GQA can eat the gain. Latent MoE shrinks the dispatched hidden state 2–4x to cut all-to-all. Dropless expert pick unbalances GPUs; a 128-expert / EP8 static map is 16 experts per card; redundant experts can prove a small extra pool balances token counts.

Train stack and philosophy: Muon/MIL vs architecture — Su Jianlin's line (whisper: 苏建磊) is that any optimizer will blow up; if you want control, change the architecture (QK logits, bounds), do not clip forever. Theseus's ship: 2017 Transformer was attention plus residual; by 2026 so many planks are swapped you can ask if it is still a Transformer. Sun's hot take: no more human-scale inventions, only refinements. Post-train: on-policy distillation turns specialist RL / reward models into teacher models and distills — easier than merging unique rewards (math, preference, extra skills) into one RL pot. Zhang also flags DenseNet / hyperconnection-era residual plumbing as the unglamorous fourth knob after attention, MoE, and the optimizer.

mental_model.name: Effective 2.8T × Architecture Episode × Distill the Teachers
mental_model.components: Scale is real only if tokens and activation match the parameter sticker. K3's sticker is 2.8T / ~100B active / 1M context and fully open. K2 was a DeepSeek-shaped scaler; K3 is where Moonshot spends architecture: hybrid attention, gated MLA, latent dispatch, redundant-expert load balance. MLA is a better MQA, not a forever primitive — V4 already left. OPD is the multi-teacher move: do not merge rewards, distill specialists. Theseus: keep swapping planks and call it incremental. Fix instability in the architecture, not only in Muon clips.
mental_model.application: Private:Moonshot is the named 2.8T open MoE and the K2-to-K3 architecture turn. Private:DeepSeek is the V3 skeleton K2 copied and the V4 lab that dropped MLA. NVDA is the GPU that waits when expert load is uneven — infra, not a new chip thesis. Do not underwrite a 2.8T press release trained on 100B tokens. Fade 'MLA is the consensus forever.' Treat OPD as the post-train org chart, not a magic loss.

key_insights.view: 2.8T is a claim about training, not a file size.
key_insights.question: What is fake scale?
key_insights.answer: Stand up 2.8T, run 100B tokens, ship. K3's tape is effective scale plus ~100B active and 1M context, open.

key_insights.question: What changed after K2?
key_insights.answer: K2 reused a DeepSeek-V3 stack. K3 adds hybrid attention, gated MLA, latent MoE. MLA is better MQA; V4 already left.

key_insights.view: Distill teachers, do not merge rewards.
key_insights.question: Why on-policy distillation?
key_insights.answer: Each RL skill has its own reward. OPD turns specialists into teachers. Easier than one pot of math plus preference plus extras.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Named 2.8T / ~100B-active open MoE with a real architecture delta vs K2; scale is only as good as the tokens — medium
The V3-class stack K2 copied, and the V4 lab that already walked off MLA — low
